title: Accounts and Records; E-way Bill
outcomes: Apply provisions on accounts and records.
Determine when an e-way bill is required.
Apply generation rules for Part A and Part B.
Compute validity and apply cancellation and acceptance rules.

meta.exam_tip: For validity, divide distance by 200 (or 20 for ODC) and round up.

concepts.title: Accounts and records
body: Section 35 requires every registered person to keep at its principal place of business true and correct accounts of production, inward and outward supplies, stock, ITC, output tax and prescribed records; electronic records are allowed with audit trail. Additional places of business must keep relevant records too.

Rule 56 prescribes registers, including separate accounts for advances, stock (with goods lost, stolen or gifted) and details of suppliers and recipients; entries must not be erased or overwritten, and corrections must be traceable.

Section 36 requires records to be retained for 72 months from the due date of the annual return for that year; where proceedings are pending, until one year after their final disposal or 72 months, whichever later. Unaccounted goods found at the place of business are deemed supplied.
concepts.analogy: Keep complete records for six years after the annual return.
concepts.work: Records for 2026-27 must be kept until December 2033.

concepts.title: When an e-way bill is required
body: Rule 138: an e-way bill is needed when goods of consignment value above ₹50,000 move by a conveyance, in relation to a supply, for reasons other than supply (e.g. stock transfer), or on inward supply from an unregistered person.

It is needed irrespective of value for inter-State movement to a job worker by a principal or registered job worker, and for inter-State movement of handicraft goods by persons exempt from registration.

Exemptions include non-motorised conveyance, goods from port or airport to ICD or customs station for clearance, goods specified in the annexure (e.g. LPG to households, fresh produce, currency), transit to or from Nepal and Bhutan, movement under customs seal, empty cargo containers, and movement within notified distances in some cases.
concepts.analogy: Value above ₹50,000 by conveyance triggers an e-way bill.
concepts.work: Inputs sent to an out-of-State job worker need an e-way bill even for ₹10,000.

concepts.title: Generation, Part A and Part B
body: Part A (supplier, recipient, place of delivery, document, value, HSN, reason) is filled by the registered consignor, consignee or an authorised transporter; Part B (vehicle number or transport document) is completed before movement. Part B is not needed where goods move up to 50 km within the State between the business place and a transporter's place.
Where goods are handed to a transporter, the transporter may generate the EWB on authorisation; ECOs and courier agencies can also furnish Part A. Unregistered transporters enrol to get a TRANSIN.
A transporter carrying multiple consignments may generate a consolidated e-way bill; vehicle changes in transit are updated in Part B.
concepts.analogy: Part A is about the goods; Part B is about the vehicle.
concepts.work: Goods taken 30 km within the State to a transporter's godown need no Part B for that leg.

concepts.title: Validity, cancellation and acceptance
body: Validity: one day up to 200 km and one extra day per 200 km or part (for over-dimensional cargo and multimodal shipments involving ships: one day per 20 km); counted to midnight of the day following generation. Validity may be extended within eight hours before or after expiry if goods cannot reach in time.

An e-way bill may be cancelled within 24 hours of generation if goods are not moved, but not once verified in transit. The recipient may accept or reject it within 72 hours of details being made available (or before delivery, if earlier); otherwise it is deemed accepted.

Rule 138B and 138C empower officers to intercept and verify; a summary report is recorded within 24 hours and a final report within three days. Detention and penalty under section 129 can follow for movement without valid documents.
concepts.analogy: Validity is distance-based; cancellation must be within 24 hours.
concepts.work: A 650 km road journey gets four days of validity.

viva.q: What happens to goods found unaccounted at the place of business?
viva.model: They are deemed supplied and tax is determined as for supplies.

viva.q: What is a consolidated e-way bill?
viva.model: A single bill generated by a transporter for multiple consignments in one conveyance, using individual EWB numbers.
Within eight hours before or after expiry when goods cannot reach in time due to exceptional circumstances.
The person causing movement or the transporter, with vehicle or transport document details.

viva.q: Can corrections in accounts overwrite earlier entries?
viva.model: Corrections are made by fresh, attested entries so that the original entry stays visible and traceable.
